requirement_text.REQ-039: GitHub issue #71. Companion (+1) registration through a companion code, with consent before storage and invited_by_user_id attribution. A code with grants_companion_of = X sets registrations.invited_by_user_id = X, one field for both mechanic and referral reporting, no schema change. The companion completes NAME, PHONE, COMPANY only, reusing REQ-030's reduced-field pattern. Consent before storage is the security-critical property. Companions occupy a normal seat, waitlisted like anyone else when full. One use unless the organizer overrides max_uses. Both guest and host are notified once each, transactionally; host notification carries name+company only, never phone/email (S3).

task.description: Rework iteration 1 of REQ-039's design in response to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's BLOCKER (handoffs/WF02-REQ-039/step-01b-code-design-validator.json): the design's own Open Question 1 (a returning bot user handed a companion code hits profiles_user_id_unique via createWalkinProfile's plain INSERT, since a companion code's issuedToUserId is always null so validateInviteCodeForRedemption's identity check never fires) was left unresolved with two undecided options. Read apps/bot/src/domain/profile.ts and apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts to confirm the exact existing function for 'does this user already have a profiles row' -- getProfileByUserId(db, userId): Promise<ProfileRecord | null>, already exported, already used by REQ-019's own resumability logic. Chose and concretely specified Option A (skip-and-redeem-immediately), not Option B (collect-and-UPDATE), for the stated reasons below.
acceptance_criteria: Pick ONE resolution (not both) and specify it concretely in the design text, not as an open question
State reasoning for which option is better, verified rather than assumed
Confirm the resolution does not reopen the pre-consent-write invariant (S1)
Reflect the resolution in AC1/AC9 of the AC map (§7)
Touch nothing else in the design

result.summary: docs/agents/design/REQ-039.md updated in four places, everything else left untouched. (1) §0's reused-pieces table gains one row: domain/profile.ts's getProfileByUserId, reused read-only. (2) §2's branch now performs a second read -- existingProfile = await getProfileByUserId(db, flowUser.id), evaluated only when the code is a companion code -- and adds existingProfile === null to the condition for entering the field-collection flow; the else branch (unconditional redeemInviteCode call) now explicitly also covers a returning guest with an existing Profile row, and a new closing paragraph states why this introduces no double-consent-collection risk: hasConsented (checked immediately above, unchanged position) is already true by construction for anyone reaching this branch, whether that became true seconds ago (new guest, just tapped consent:agree) or on a prior visit (returning guest) -- S1 is satisfied identically either way, and this branch only ever changes whether the REDUCED-FIELD PROFILE conversation runs, never whether consent is collected. (3) §5 point 4 is rewritten: chosen resolution is Option A (skip-and-redeem-immediately) as the primary mechanism via §2's existingProfile check, backstopped at the write itself by changing createWalkinProfile's call site for this feature to use .onConflictDoNothing({ target: profiles.userId }) instead of a plain INSERT -- guards the pre-transaction read's staleness (a race between the read and the transaction committing) the same way resolveOrCreateUser's own onConflictDoUpdate on tg_id already guards user-row creation. Option B (collect-and-UPDATE) is explicitly named and rejected: it would let a raced/late field-collection write silently overwrite a returning guest's richer, previously-collected REQ-019 profile data (position/experienceLevel/isStudent/email/links -- fields this reduced flow never asks about) with blanks or stale values; DO NOTHING instead leaves any existing row untouched, at the cost only of a wasted conversation for that one guest, never data loss or a crash. (4) Open Questions #1 is marked RESOLVED (rework 1) with a summary of both the primary mechanism and the backstop, and §7's AC1 and AC9 rows are updated to state the resolution holds identically for the returning-guest branch (invited_by_user_id is set unconditionally in §5 point 3 regardless of companionProfile; exactly one AuditLog row is written whether the Profile INSERT succeeds or no-ops).
issues: Open Questions #2 (re-redemption, not actually open), #3 (function file placement), #4 (callback_data string / catalog copy), #5 (event-title-in-prompt copy) are unchanged from the original design -- CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already ruled these legitimately deferrable to BACKEND-DEV/CONTENT-BA, not blocking, and this rework did not touch them.
